text:
Marathon Petroleum is up a tiny fraction today, but that move is part of a much larger 13% rally over the past two weeks. The driver has been a sharp reversal in geopolitical risk: oil prices had spiked earlier in October when Iran escalated attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, hitting $110+ for Brent crude, but that rally collapsed on October 19th when Trump announced sanctions relief on Russian energy, raising hopes that more crude would flow into global markets and ease supply tightness. For a refiner like Marathon, lower crude prices and rising supply mean cheaper feedstock and better margins—exactly what the recent surge reflects.

The refining backdrop supports this narrative: U.S. refineries are running at 93.5% capacity with healthy fuel inventories, so the sector is positioned to benefit when crude costs fall. The shift from geopolitical panic to sanctions relief is a real regime change for energy investors, and Marathon has been along for the ride.
